title: Stripe’s AI Strategy: Build More, Not Less
thesis: This episode argues that Stripe is successfully transforming from a payments company into a comprehensive financial infrastructure platform by building more products rather than the same things with fewer people. The thesis relies on the claim that AI is making engineers dramatically more productive, allowing Stripe to capture high-standard startups and enterprise clients while growing signups and revenue significantly.

claims.claim: The speaker is bullish on AI making engineers dramatically more productive and states that Stripe's response is to build more, not the same things with fewer people.
claims.quote: I'm very bullish on AI is making engineers dramatically more productive. Stripes response isn't to build the same things with fewer people. It's to build more.

claims.claim: The average AI company uses 11 different Stripe products, and Stripe has launched 288 distinct products.
claims.quote: And at sessions, I believe you had 288 distinct product launches. So I want to talk about velocity also, but just to start with just what is the state of Stripe today?

claims.claim: Stripe has inverted its value proposition from being a payments company with add-ons to being a multi-product platform focusing on financial infrastructure.
claims.quote: So internally, we think about Stripe as having inverted our value proposition from being a payments company with sort of add-ons. So now being this multi-product platform, where everything sort of focuses on financial infrastructure

claims.claim: Stripe has reduced frictions and increased agency to help businesses grow by reducing friction and increasing agency to be more agile with their business model.
claims.quote: helping you grow by reducing the friction and increasing the agency to be more agile with your business model, to operate in more countries, and just go faster when it comes to everything that touches revenue and cash.

claims.claim: Stripe has gone from payments to billing, subscriptions, invoicing, connect, radar, tax, and has around 25-30 products headlining branded products.
claims.quote: So just practically speaking, went from payments to then billing, subscriptions, and invoicing, connect if you're a platformer marketplace, radar, from making fraud, radar now for doing many more things than that, tax, just I think we don't actually count, but somewhere in and around 25, 30 products

claims.claim: Stripe has captured companies like DoorDash and Instaclared when they were in YC and grew with them along the way.
claims.quote: And then famously, part of the beauty of Stripe's growth and business model is that you captured companies like DoorDash and Instaclared when they were in YC. And then you grew with them along the way.

claims.claim: Startups have the highest standards of all of Stripe's customers, and once Stripe starts working with startups, they want to work with them forever.
claims.quote: So on another subtle reason to win all the startups and win them again is they actually have the highest standards of all of our customers. I looked recently at the CSAP for Stripe's reporting and for our very, very large enterprise users, your reporting is great. We love the data you give us.

claims.claim: Stripe has worked with 400-500 companies, including Amazon and Microsoft at the enterprise level.
claims.quote: 4 to 500 companies. We work, of course, with the Amazon's and the world, Microsoft's and at the enterprise, it's sort of a different sales cycle. It's a different post-sale activation motion.

claims.quote: So I think you guys publicly said that first half signups grew 50% year over years. And that the median 26th cohort is generating 50% more revenue than the comparable 25 cohort.
